keyEvents.impact: Marxist military rule, Red Terror and famine

keyEvents.event: EPRDF victory and Eritrea's de facto independence
keyEvents.impact: Ethnic federalism under Tigrayan-led rule; Ethiopia became landlocked when Eritrea seceded in 1993
Around 80,000 dead and a frozen hostility that lasted two decades

keyEvents.impact: Nobel Peace Prize, political opening and the sidelining of the TPLF

keyEvents.event: Tigray war begins (with Eritrean forces fighting alongside federal troops)
keyEvents.impact: Hundreds of thousands killed by war and famine before the 2022 Pretoria agreement

keyEvents.event: Somaliland port MoU, Amhara Fano insurgency and floating of the birr under an IMF program
keyEvents.impact: Sea-access ambitions alarmed neighbours while the economy was painfully liberalized
National triumph and leverage over the Nile; Egypt and Sudan called it an existential threat

keyEvents.event: Prosperity Party landslide (June), Abiy's new term (October) and renewed war in Tigray from late September with Eritrean troops reported inside Tigray
keyEvents.impact: Pretoria peace collapsed; Abiy's Red Sea and Assab rhetoric raises the risk of interstate war with Eritrea

history.narrative: Africa's second most populous country, an ancient empire turned fractious ethnic federation, ruled by a prime minister who sees sovereign Red Sea access as a historic mission. The Nile dam is its pride and Egypt's fear; Tigray, Amhara and Eritrea are its open wounds.

redLines.description: Secession of Tigray or foreign (Eritrean) occupation of Ethiopian territory
Military threat to the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
Permanent denial of access to the Red Sea through Djibouti, Eritrea or Somaliland

internalDivisions.name: Tigrayan TPLF forces at war with Addis Ababa again since September 2026
Amhara Fano insurgency against the federal government
Oromo grievances and the OLA insurgency

goals.description: Crush the renewed Tigray rebellion and the Fano insurgency to hold the federation together
Secure sovereign Red Sea access, through negotiation or pressure on Eritrea's port of Assab
Protect the Renaissance Dam and resist Egyptian-led encirclement with Eritrea and Somalia
Complete IMF-backed reforms and sustain high growth for a fast-growing population
